subject: Milva McDonald City Council Candidacy
overview: City Council candidate Milva McDonald appeared on the Medford Bytes podcast to discuss her background, her leadership on the Medford Charter Review Commission, and her platform for the upcoming municipal election.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Background
items.summary: Milva McDonald introduced herself as a West Medford resident, former Boston Globe journalist, and current jazz publicist running for City Council.

items.title: Favorite Local Food
items.summary: McDonald highlighted the Medford Farmers Market as her favorite spot to source local food, citing snap benefits and the variety of vendors.

items.title: Candidacy Motivation and Charter Review Work
items.summary: McDonald explained how her immigrant mother's work ethic and her own experience chairing the Medford Charter Review Commission inspired her to run for office.

items.title: Charter Reform and Ward Representation
items.summary: McDonald discussed the importance of the proposed charter reforms, emphasizing how ward-based representation would lower barriers for local candidates and improve representation.

items.title: Campaign Platform and Priorities
items.summary: McDonald outlined her legislative priorities, which include zoning reform to increase housing and the tax base, affordable housing trust funding, traffic calming, and hiring a City Hall arts coordinator.

items.title: Political Alignment and Independence
items.summary: McDonald noted that she entered the race late and chose to run as an independent, though she aligns with many progressive policy goals.

items.title: Proposal for an LGBTQ+ Commission
items.summary: McDonald proposed establishing a municipal LGBTQ+ commission to advocate for equality, visibility, and community building year-round.

items.title: Upcoming Campaign Events
items.summary: McDonald shared details for upcoming music-themed campaign events at Mrs. Murphy's pub and provided her website and social media contact details.
